skills.name: Scalar and vector quantities; measuring force

note.text:
A scalar quantity has size (magnitude) only: mass, time, distance, speed, temperature, energy.
A vector quantity has size and direction: force, weight, displacement, velocity, acceleration.
Forces are measured in newtons (N) with a newton meter (spring balance). A beam balance compares masses.
Combining forces along a line: same direction → add; opposite directions → subtract, and the resultant acts in the direction of the larger force.
Two forces at right angles: the resultant is found with Pythagoras.

sections.heading: Size only, or size and direction?
sections.text:
Some quantities are fully described by a number and a unit: a mass of {50} kg, a time of {12} s, a temperature of {30} °C. These are scalars.
Others also need a direction: a force of {20} N to the left, a displacement of {3} km north. These are vectors.
Weight is a vector: it is a force and it always acts downwards, towards the centre of the Earth.

sections.heading: Measuring force
sections.text:
A newton meter (spring balance) has a spring that stretches when you pull it; the scale shows the force in newtons (N).
A beam balance compares an unknown mass with known masses. It gives mass, not force, so it reads the same on the Moon.
In the laboratory, handle these instruments gently: overloading a spring damages it.

sections.heading: Adding forces
sections.text:
Forces on the same line combine simply:
• same direction: add them ({6} N + {4} N = {10} N);
• opposite directions: subtract, and the resultant acts in the direction of the larger force ({6} N east and {4} N west give {2} N east).
Forces at right angles combine like the sides of a right-angled triangle: {3} N east and {4} N north give a resultant of {5} N.

key_words.meaning: a quantity with size and direction
the single force with the same effect as several forces

examples: {8} N and {8} N in opposite directions: resultant {0} N

mistake.wrong: {6} N east and {4} N west give {10} N
mistake.why: Forces in opposite directions work against each other: subtract them.

worked_example.problem: Two boys pull a cart: one with {a} N to the east, the other with {b} N to the west. Find the resultant force.
steps: The larger force is to the east, so the resultant is {a - b} N to the east.

cards.idea: A vector has a direction; a scalar does not.
example: Force {20} N upwards is a vector; a mass of {20} kg is a scalar.

cards.idea: A newton meter measures force in newtons.
example: The spring stretches more for a bigger pull.

cards.idea: Forces in the same direction add; in opposite directions they subtract.
example: {6} N and {4} N east: {10} N east. {6} N east and {4} N west: {2} N east.

check.prompt: Forces of {a} N and {b} N act on a box {X.d}. Find the size of the resultant force (N).

misconceptions.explain: {X.s == 1 ? 'In the same direction the forces add.' : 'In opposite directions one force cancels part of the other: subtract.'}

solution: {X.s == 1 ? a + ' + ' + b : max(a, b) + ' − ' + min(a, b)} = {answer} N.

pick.q: A {20} N force pulls a box east and a {35} N force pulls it west. What is the resultant?
e: The larger force is to the west, so the resultant points west.
Opposite directions: subtract, and the larger force decides the direction.
pick.y: 35 − 20 = 15 N, in the direction of the larger force.

pick.q: Two equal forces of {10} N pull a rope in opposite directions. What is the resultant?
e: They act in opposite directions: subtract.
pick.y: Equal and opposite forces are balanced: no resultant.

pick.q: A {50} N push forward and {50} N friction act on a cart. The cart…
w: has a resultant of 50 N forward
has a resultant of 50 N backward
e: Friction acts in the opposite direction: subtract.
The push and friction are equal.

misconceptions.explain: At right angles the forces do not simply add: use Pythagoras.
At right angles use Pythagoras: R² = a² + b².

solution: The forces are at right angles: use Pythagoras.
